battle.name: 黑鷹戰爭
battle.theater: 密西西比河上游搖石河走廊
battle.brief: 黑鷹率蘇克、梅斯夸基同基卡普人越過密西西比河重返伊利諾伊，聯邦軍同州民兵沿搖石河追擊，由斯提爾曼河打到威斯康辛高地，最後喺壞斧河以汽船炮火封河。戰爭始於1832年4月5日，8月2日壞斧河決戰後收場。卡面輪發手槍早被燧發槍淘汰，佢喺此役嘅位置係制度位置：佢確立嘅軍官側身手槍，到1832年就係義勇騎兵手上嗰支燧發手槍。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 聯邦一方分正規軍與民兵兩套指揮系統。正規軍隸西部軍區，1831年由埃德蒙·蓋恩斯少將統轄，1832年4月改由准將亨利·阿特金森接手；阿特金森自密蘇里傑斐遜兵營乘汽船溯密西西比河而上，4月12日抵羅克島阿姆斯特朗堡，再以629名正規步兵與3196名騎兵義勇編成「邊疆軍」，義勇分三旅，由亞歷山大·波西、米爾頓·亞歷山大、詹姆斯·亨利三位旅長率領。民兵方面，伊利諾伊州長約翰·雷諾茲4月22日在比爾茲敦召集2100名志願者，編為五團加一個偵察營，由塞繆爾·懷特賽德准將統率。總統傑克遜6月15日派溫菲爾德·斯科特自東部調兵接防，七月底抵芝加哥時已因霍亂銳減。聯邦另組原住民盟友序列：梅諾米尼、達科他與部分霍奇克、波塔瓦托米人由瓦巴沙、拉爾克帶領，名義上歸民兵上校威廉·漢密爾頓指揮，實際各自作戰。蘇克一方則由黑鷹、尼波、瓦波克希克等首領率領的聯盟，包含蘇克、梅斯夸基、基卡普三大族，另有霍奇克與波塔瓦托米人少量加入；反對開戰嘅基奧卡克一派留在密西西比河以西，佢同瓦佩洛成為聯邦談判時嘅蘇克代表。
countriesEn: The federal side ran two separate command systems: regular army and militia. The regulars belonged to the Western Department, commanded in 1831 by Major General Edmund P. Gaines and taken over in April 1832 by Brigadier General Henry Atkinson. Atkinson steamed up the Mississippi from Jefferson Barracks in Missouri, reached Fort Armstrong on Rock Island on 12 April, and organized an "Army of the Frontier" of 629 regular infantry and 3,196 mounted militia volunteers, the volunteers being divided into three brigades under Alexander Posey, Milton Alexander and James D. Henry. On the militia side, Governor John Reynolds of Illinois called up 2,100 volunteers at Beardstown on 22 April, organized into five regiments and a scout battalion under Brigadier General Samuel Whiteside. President Jackson sent Winfield Scott eastwards on 15 June to take over, and by the time Scott reached Chicago at the end of July his command had been thinned by cholera. The federal side also organized a Native auxiliary column: Menominee, Dakota and some Ho-Chunk and Potawatomi warriors led by Wabasha and L'Arc, nominally under the militia Colonel William S. Hamilton, though in practice they fought on their own terms. The Sauk side was the coalition led by Black Hawk, Neapope and Wabokieshiek, drawn from the Sauk, Meskwaki and Kickapoo nations, with a small number of Ho-Chunk and Potawatomi joining. The peace faction under Keokuk stayed west of the Mississippi, and Keokuk together with Wapello became the Sauk representatives in the federal treaty councils.
people: 黑鷹六十多歲，1812年戰爭已經同美國交過手，1829年成為蘇克族主張抵抗的一派領袖；他同基奧卡克都唔係文職首領，一個主戰、一個主遷，族群內部嘅分裂正係呢場戰爭嘅人事底色。瓦波克希克即「白人雲」係先知，母系屬霍奇克、父系出蘇克族世襲首領族群，加入黑鷹一夥後成為隊內最高文職首領，先知村就係以佢命名；尼波從加拿大馬爾登堡帶返「英方同其他部落都會支援」嘅假情報，直接令黑鷹高估咗自己嘅處境，戰後佢自己都批評尼波誤導。聯邦方面，阿特金森係一個未打過仗、習慣用文書處理戰事嘅指揮官；真正在前線做決定嘅係紮卡里·泰勒、傑斐遜·戴維斯、詹姆斯·克萊曼、亨利·道奇同詹姆斯·亨利，溫菲爾德·斯科特就遲到未能參戰。印地安事務官系統亦左右全局：托馬斯·福賽斯早前被傑克遜換走，費利克斯·聖弗蘭接任，談判同情報質素一路下跌。23歲嘅亞伯拉罕·林肯當選民兵連長，隨軍行軍但冇參加戰鬥；同樣參戰嘅蘇克支持者基奧卡克，就成為日後兩族保留地談判嘅主角。
peopleEn: Black Hawk was in his sixties and had already fought the Americans in the War of 1812; in 1829 he emerged as the leader of the Sauk faction that resisted American encroachment. Neither he nor Keokuk was a civil chief: one advocated war, the other removal, and that split inside the tribe is the human fault line running under the whole conflict. Wabokieshiek, known to the Americans as White Cloud, was a shaman whose mother was Ho-Chunk and whose father belonged to the Sauk clan that supplied civil chiefs; once he joined Black Hawk he became the senior civil chief of the band, and Prophetstown was named for him. Neapope brought back from Fort Malden in Canada the false report that the British and the other tribes were ready to support the Sauks, and it was this report that made Black Hawk overestimate his position, a claim he himself criticized afterwards. On the federal side Atkinson was a paper commander, used to handling operations through paperwork and with no combat experience of his own; the men actually making decisions in the field were Zachary Taylor, Jefferson Davis, James Clyman, Henry Dodge and James D. Henry, while Winfield Scott arrived too late to take part. The Indian agent system mattered just as much: Thomas Forsyth had been replaced under Jackson by Felix St. Vrain, and the quality of both negotiation and intelligence declined accordingly. Twenty-three-year-old Abraham Lincoln was elected captain of a militia company and marched with the army but saw no combat. Keokuk, the Sauk supporter who had stayed out of the fighting, later became the central figure in the treaty councils over the two tribes' reservation.
kits: 聯邦正規軍用1816同1819型燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約.54，後膛裝填，軍官配1817、1822同1831型燧發手槍，騎兵用1822型龍騎馬刀；民兵以獵槍、散彈槍為主，騎兵義勇用獵槍加手槍加馬刀，汽船Warrior號裝一門旋轉小炮做河上封鎖火力，軍需靠馬車、牛車同密西西比河上的汽船供應。蘇克聯軍嘅槍械主要係英法商人經聖路易斯流入嘅歐洲燧發步槍同自用獵槍，冷兵器則係弓箭、斧頭、長矛、皮盾同護腕。卡面嗰件輪發手槍要擺正位置：西班牙造、1500年前後嘅設計，係最早嘅後膛手槍，但機件價錢高、要專門甲匠保養，十七世紀末已經畀燧發槍淘汰，到1832年只會出現喺武庫清冊、軍官收藏或者古董商嘅櫥窗，唔會出現喺斯提爾曼河、威斯康辛高地或壞斧河嘅火線上。佢喺呢場戰爭真正嘅位置係制度位置：佢確立咗「後膛手槍係軍官同近衛專用嘅側身武器」呢個做法，到1832年落到美軍同州民兵手上，就係1831型燧發手槍；而黑鷹1832年喺華盛頓俾人畫像時，身上亦係歐式軍裝加一支燧發手槍同一把軍刀，同一件象徵，敵我兩邊都有份。
kitsEn: Federal regulars carried the Model 1816 and Model 1819 flintlock smoothbore muskets of about .54 calibre, loaded at the breech, with Model 1817, 1822 and 1831 flintlock pistols issued to officers and the Model 1822 dragoon sabre for mounted troops. Militia units relied mostly on hunting rifles and shotguns, while mounted volunteers carried hunting rifles with pistols and sabres; the steamboat Warrior mounted a swivel gun for river interdiction, and the commissariat drew on wagons, ox carts and the steamboats on the Mississippi. The Sauk coalition obtained its firearms chiefly from European flintlock trade muskets and hunting rifles that British and French merchants carried up the Missouri to St. Louis, and its cold weapons were bows, axes, lances, hide shields and wrist guards. The card piece has to be placed correctly: the wheel-lock pistol, Spanish in origin and dating from around 1500, was the earliest true breech-loading handgun, but its mechanism was expensive and needed a specialist armourer, and it had been displaced by the flintlock from the late seventeenth century; by 1832 it would appear only in armoury inventories, in officers' collections or in an antique dealer's window, never on the firing line at Stillman's Run, Wisconsin Heights or Bad Axe. Its real position in this war is institutional: it established the idea of the breech-loading handgun as a sidearm reserved for officers and bodyguards, and by 1832 that idea had reached the US army and the state militia in the form of the Model 1831 flintlock pistol. When Black Hawk was painted in Washington in 1832 he likewise wore European-style dress with a flintlock pistol and a sword, so that the same symbol was present on both sides of the fight.
tactics: 民兵以縱隊沿搖石河推進，五月十日燒掉空村先知村，再溯河約四十英里到迪克森渡口等阿特金森；斯提爾曼河之戰就係一次黃昏突襲，營地被打散。之後聯邦由縱隊追擊改為分散搜索，同時用騎兵義勇包抄落後突擊隊：道奇率二十九名騎兵追到佩卡托尼卡河彎道，將約十一名突擊者全部解決。黑鷹本人兩度圍攻民兵木寨，蘋果河堡守軍只二十至三十五人，由寨內婦女裝藥壓彈，堅守約四十五分鐘，逼得攻方退走；第二次凱洛格林戰役圍攻約兩小時，蘇克聯軍死九人、民兵死五人，呢場係黑鷹最後一次軍事成功。七月二十一日威斯康辛高地，黑鷹以五十名蘇克戰士加六七十名基卡普人擋住七百五十名民兵作後衛戰，傷亡遠大於對方，但成功拖到非戰鬥員過河。八月一日汽船Warrior號沿密西西比河用炮火封鎖渡口，翌日登岸部隊配合聯邦盟友原住民自陸路夾擊，把最後一批人逼落水。補給線係全場最弱一環：民兵糧秣短缺、正規軍糧草告罄，斯科特嘅部隊沿途死于霍亂，為追擊而拉長嘅縱隊幾乎斷線。
tacticsEn: The militia pushed up the Rock River in column, burned the empty village of Prophetstown on 10 May, and then marched some forty miles upstream to Dixon's Ferry to await Atkinson; the battle of Stillman's Run was a dusk assault that scattered the camp. Thereafter the federal side abandoned the single marching column for scattered searching and used mounted volunteers to cut off raiding parties: Dodge took twenty-nine mounted men after one raid and destroyed about eleven attackers at a bend of the Pecatonica. Black Hawk twice assaulted the settlers' blockhouse defences himself. At Apple River Fort the garrison numbered only twenty to thirty-five, with the women inside loading the muskets and moulding bullets, and held out for about forty-five minutes before the attackers withdrew. The second fight at Kellogg's Grove lasted about two hours, costing the Sauk coalition nine warriors against five militia dead, and it was Black Hawk's last military success. At Wisconsin Heights on 21 July he held up some seven hundred and fifty militiamen with fifty Sauk warriors and sixty to seventy Kickapoos in a rearguard action that cost him far more than it cost the Americans, but it bought time for the non-combatants to cross the river. On 1 August the steamboat Warrior used its gun to interdict the crossing on the Mississippi, and the next day a landing party worked with allied Native auxiliaries from the landward side to pin the last of the band at the water's edge. Supply was the weakest link of the entire campaign: militia rations ran short, regular army supplies ran out, Scott's men died of cholera along the route, and the columns stretched by pursuit came close to breaking their line of communication altogether.
data: 人口基數：1832年蘇克同梅斯夸基兩族合計約六千人，黑鷹一派只係其中約八百人，1831年一度聚到一千五百人；1832年4月5日越境者為約五百名戰士加六百名非戰鬥員，到壞斧河時只剩約五百人、其中約一百五十名戰士。聯邦兵員：首批民兵2100人，伊利諾伊一州參戰民兵估計六千至七千人，邊疆軍為629名正規加3196名騎兵義勇，斯科特六月自東部調950人，抵芝加哥時只剩約350名有效兵力。戰果：斯提爾曼河之戰係40名戰士對12名民兵陣亡、自方死3人；佩卡托尼卡河彎道29名騎兵全殲約11名突擊者；凱洛格林兩役民兵死3人、原住民死3人，同區另一場死3名民兵同5至6名原住民；威斯康辛高地民兵死1人、原住民死多達68人；八月一日Warrior號炮擊打死23名原住民、美軍僅1人受傷。地價：1804年條約代價只係2200多美元貨物加每年1000美元貨物；1832年9月霍奇克條約割出威斯康辛河以南土地，換愛荷華一條40英里地帶加每年一萬美元共27年；隨後蘇克條約出讓東愛荷華約六百萬英畝，換每年二萬美元共三十年。距離：Saukenuk至先知村約35英里，壞斧河口在密西西比河下游數英里。
dataEn: Population base: in 1832 the Sauk and Meskwaki together numbered about six thousand people, of whom Black Hawk's faction was only some eight hundred, though the following had grown to about fifteen hundred in 1831. The band that crossed into Illinois on 5 April 1832 counted roughly five hundred warriors and six hundred non-combatants, and by Bad Axe it had shrunk to about five hundred people, of whom around a hundred and fifty were warriors. Federal numbers: an initial muster of 2,100 militia, an estimated six to seven thousand Illinois militia in the campaign as a whole, an Army of the Frontier of 629 regulars and 3,196 mounted volunteers, and 950 troops Scott drew from the eastern army in June, of whom only about 350 were still effective when he reached Chicago. Results: at Stillman's Run forty warriors killed twelve militia and lost three of their own; at the bend of the Pecatonica, twenty-nine mounted men destroyed about eleven raiders; the two fights at Kellogg's Grove cost three militia and three Native dead, and a nearby engagement on the same day three militia and five or six Natives; at Wisconsin Heights one militiaman fell against as many as sixty-eight Native dead; and on 1 August the gun of the Warrior killed twenty-three Natives while a single soldier aboard was wounded. Land values: the 1804 treaty bought a vast tract for goods worth a little over two thousand two hundred dollars plus a thousand dollars of goods every year; the September 1832 Ho-Chunk treaty ceded everything south of the Wisconsin River in exchange for a forty-mile strip in Iowa and ten thousand dollars a year for twenty-seven years; the later Sauk treaty ceded about six million acres in eastern Iowa for twenty thousand dollars a year for thirty years. Distances: roughly thirty-five miles from Saukenuk to Prophetstown, with the mouth of the Bad Axe a few miles downstream on the Mississippi.
cause: 1804年《聖路易斯條約》由威廉·亨利·哈里森代表政府同蘇克、梅斯夸基首領簽訂，以區區代價買下密西西比河以東大片土地，但簽約首領未經族群議會授權，書面條款同口頭所講有出入，兩族要到多年後先知道自己賣咗幾多。1828年政府開始測量賣地，1829年黑鷹一派回到Saukenuk，發現聚落已被定居者佔住；1830年尼波從英方帶回「各族都會支援」嘅消息，令黑鷹相信可以靠談判爭回原地。1831年6月30日黑鷹同蓋恩斯簽署留喺密西西比河以西嘅協議，但英方情報顯示英國唔會介入，潛在盟友波塔瓦托米人亦喺五月一日芝加哥議會宣告支持黑鷹即係叛族。聯邦方面則認定武裝集團意圖攻擊，5月14日斯提爾曼河之戰之後，懷特賽德、傑克遜同國防部長路易斯·卡斯都拒絕再談，決定要用一次決定性勝利震懾其他族群。民兵一邊同年輕戰士一邊雙方都想要一場仗，談判空間被壓到最細，最細一步就爆。
causeEn: The Treaty of St. Louis of 1804 was negotiated by William Henry Harrison on behalf of the government with Sauk and Meskwaki leaders, and it bought a vast tract east of the Mississippi for a trifling consideration; but the signers had no authorization from the tribal councils, the written terms did not match what was said aloud, and the two nations did not learn the full extent of the cession until years later. In 1828 the government began surveying the land for sale, and in 1829 Black Hawk's faction returned to Saukenuk to find the settlement occupied by squatters. In 1830 Neapope returned with the report that the British and the other tribes were ready to help, and Black Hawk came to believe he could negotiate his way back to his own country. On 30 June 1831 Black Hawk and Gaines signed an agreement to remain west of the Mississippi, but the British position showed no intervention was coming, and the prospective allies gave up as well: a Potawatomi council outside Chicago on 1 May 1832 resolved that any Potawatomi who supported Black Hawk was a traitor to the tribe. The federal authorities meanwhile had convinced themselves that the armed band intended an attack, and after the fight at Stillman's Run on 14 May, Whiteside, Jackson and Secretary of War Lewis Cass all refused further negotiation and resolved on a resounding victory to discourage the other tribes. On the militia side and among the young warriors of the band, both parties wanted a fight, and the space for diplomacy narrowed until a single misstep set it off.
impact: 呢場戰爭係舊西北地區原住民武裝抵抗嘅終點。此後聯邦以「一個部分出走並開戰、整個民族都要負責」為由，向蘇克、梅斯夸基、霍奇克同波塔瓦托米各部逐一收地，1830年《印第安人遷移法》由口號變成行政程序；蘇克最後一塊愛荷華保留地1836年賣出，1842年再賣尾地，多數族人遷往堪薩斯保留地。蘇克、達科他同梅諾米尼之間為獵場打咗幾十年嘅糾紛，隨住聯邦介入而收束，中西部獵場逐步變成耕地、礦區同運河。文化上，黑鷹被做成「高貴野蠻人」形象，由聯邦帶去巴爾的摩、費城同紐約遊覽，4月26日喺華盛頓與傑克遜短暫會面，並且成為原住民抵抗嘅象徵；史學者提醒，呢種神話化敘事同時替美國人卸走咗責任。反過來講，呢場戰爭亦係幾個美國軍人嘅跳板：斯科特喺同年升任陸軍少將，紮卡里·泰勒同傑斐遜·戴維斯亦由此踏上軍途，亞伯拉罕·林肯喺伊利諾伊民兵做過連長，日後嘅從政生涯亦由呢段經歷起點。戰役過程嘅編年、命令同軍需細節，後來成為美軍條例、供應制度同後膛手槍配發方式嘅一批教材。
impactEn: The war was the end of armed Native resistance in the Old Northwest. The federal government then worked through the Sauks, Meskwakis, Ho-Chunk and Potawatomi band by band, on the doctrine that if a part of a nation leaves the country and makes war the whole nation is responsible, and the Indian Removal Act of 1830 hardened from policy into administration. The last Sauk reservation in Iowa was sold in 1836, the remainder in 1842, and most of the people moved to a reservation in Kansas. Decades of feuding among the Sauks, Dakotas and Menominees over hunting grounds ended as the federal government took over as mediator, and the Midwestern hunting country turned progressively into farmland, mine workings and canal corridors. Culturally, Black Hawk was turned into the "noble savage", was taken on a tour of Baltimore, Philadelphia and New York, met President Jackson in Washington on 26 April, and became a lasting symbol of Native resistance; historians warn that this mythologising also relieved Americans of responsibility. In the other direction the war was a stepping stone for several US soldiers: Scott was promoted to brigadier general within the year, Zachary Taylor and Jefferson Davis began their careers, and Abraham Lincoln had already served as a militia company captain in Illinois before his political career. The campaign's correspondence, orders and supply details later entered the textbooks of American army regulation, logistics and the issue of sidearms.

resultEn: After the decision at Bad Axe on 2 August the band was scattered and its main body could not cross the Mississippi. Black Hawk and Wabokieshiek took a few dozen people north in the hope of reaching the Ojibwe, and on 27 August surrendered at Prairie du Chien to the Indian agent Joseph Street; the prisoners were taken into the custody of Colonel Zachary Taylor and sent up the Missouri to Jefferson Barracks under Lieutenants Jefferson Davis and Robert Anderson. Black Hawk and nineteen other leaders were imprisoned, and in April 1833 they were transferred to Fort Monroe in Virginia; from 4 June they were taken on a tour of Baltimore, Philadelphia and New York before being released and allowed to return west. The treaties followed at once: in September Scott and Reynolds concluded an agreement with the Ho-Chunk at Rock Island, and then a further one with the Sauks and Meskwakis represented by Keokuk and Wapello, ceding about six million acres in eastern Iowa. Keokuk was recognised as the principal chief of the two nations and granted a reservation, which was sold together with the remaining land in 1836. Among the prisoners, Wabokieshiek and Neapope were also held and were likewise released after a few months. Armed Sauk resistance east of the Mississippi ended there, and the Old Northwest saw nothing of the same scale again; the Seminole wars that began in Florida some years later carried the same line of resistance forward in a different setting.
